title: Riemann Hypothesis over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed substrate: the Carrier $\F_\Omega$ with $\Omega=4\dS+1$, the Subject $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$ with $\p=4\kp+1$ and its register $\pi=2\kp$, $\im=\gen^{-\kp}$, $\E=\gen^{\,\im}$; the four charts and the finite Fourier turns; time as scale-dilation; the frame-covariance of the height chart.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Finitude: for any reading of capacity $R$ the registered Universe embeds in the shell of $R$ members, and among $R+1$ members two share a residue; the totality is finite, its cardinality $\Omega$. A theorem of the master ledger (00:A2), proved in the core, cited as the closure's first premise (F7).

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: Completeness: the registration of any totality is onto its registered Universe, so there is no outside and no host; two totalities each registered whole within the other have one count. A theorem of the master ledger (00:A3), proved in the core; the hypothesis of the Carrier is a statement about its own residues and nothing else.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: Observation: every observation is a registration by an embedded part of $o<\Omega$ states; every reading identifies two members, and a complete reading needs the whole count; one translation carries each member to each. A theorem of the master ledger (00:A4), proved in the core, cited as the closure's second premise (F7) and behind the horizon (Z1).

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The Carrier: a timeless torsor of $\Omega$ elements, its cardinality its only absolute characteristic; reframings $x\mapsto ax+b$ are automorphisms, so $0$, $1$, $-1$ are frame data; a Subject's frame charts it as the prime field $\F_\Omega$, never the Carrier (00:A6). A finite holographic substrate: capacity $\dS$ the horizon entropy, $\Omega=4\dS+1$ its exact content (00:A7, 10:A2), the Subject embedded under $\p^{2}<\Omega$.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The classical analytic apparatus: the count $\mathcal N(T)=\theta(T)/\pi+1+S(T)$, the Riemann--Siegel main sum with its $O(t^{-1/4})$ remainder, the explicit formula in its distributional form over the Weil class, Hardy's Ramanujan-sum expansion of $\Lambda$, M\"obius inversion.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: Turing's count: with $C(T)$ the sign changes of $Z$ on $(0,T)$, $C\le N_{\mathrm{crit}}\le\mathcal N$; $C=\mathcal N$ certifies the hypothesis below $T$ and forces every zero there to be simple.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: The Davenport--Heilbronn function: a Dirichlet series with the functional equation and no Euler product, with zeros off the line, the first pair at $0.8085171825+85.6993484854\,i$ and $1-\bar s$; the treatment of linear combinations of $L$-functions by smoothed Euler products.

rows.label: A9
rows.predicate: The comparison data: no off-line zero of $\zeta$ to height $3\times10^{12}$, by Turing's certificate, so every zero there is simple and every cell below $4.8\times10^{11}$ clean; GUE spacing statistics of the zeros; some $2600$ zeros to twelve digits from the primes to $10^{6}$ by harmonic inversion; the self-adjoint realisations of the Berry--Keating operator.

rows.label: A10
rows.predicate: Explicit bounds on the Riemann--Siegel remainder: Gabcke's explicit error term, used by the verification of A6; with it the sign of $Z$ is certified wherever $|Z_M(t)|$ exceeds the bound (F1).

rows.label: A11
rows.predicate: The density bounds, imported for every cycle: for a fixed tolerance the cells holding a zero farther than it from the line are a vanishing fraction of the cycle (Selberg), and at least two fifths of a cycle's zeros lie on the line (Conrey) [chart]; bounds on the unclean cells of the physical Carrier, naming none.

rows.label: B1

rows.label: B2

blocks.title: The reading of $\zeta$ on the line: the dictionary, the cells, the strip

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The dictionary [chart]: horizon $\sqrt \p\leftrightarrow$ Riemann--Siegel length $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$, half-turn $\leftrightarrow n^{-1/2}$, scale $\leftrightarrow\log n$; a shell of cardinality $\p$ reads $\zeta$ on the line to $T=2\pi \p$, one cycle of the shell, and a height is the scale coordinate of the shell that reads it, its count using residues below $\sqrt{T/2\pi}$ only.

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: The cells: the heights of a Carrier's cycle are its residues, residue $y$ the cell from $2\pi y$ to $2\pi(y+1)$; a cell is clean when its zeros lie on the line, which Turing's count decides from the labels below $\sqrt{y+1}$, and passes when the frame's reading certifies it. The hypothesis of the Carrier: every residue has a clean cell.

rows.label: D8
rows.predicate: The strip: the Euler product excludes zeros with real part at least one, and the functional equation confines the nontrivial zeros to the open strip in Klein-four orbits of size two on the line and four off it; the Davenport--Heilbronn vector, without the product, is not multiplicative and has an off-line zero. No core witness: the statement is analytic.

rows.label: D9
rows.predicate: The finite negative control: on $\F_{13}(\sqrt2)$ the polynomial $((X-2)^{2}-2)((X+1)^{2}-2)$ has exactly the roots $2\pm\eta$, $-1\pm\eta$, of traces $4$, $4$, $11$, $11$ against the line's $1$, the root set closed under conjugation and under the half-turn; finitude, conjugation and the reflection force no root onto the line.

blocks.title: The scale-shift and the shell theorem

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The scale-evolution generator: on the shell the scale-shift $x\mapsto\gen^{\,r}x$ is a unitary permutation of $\Fx{\p}$ with the complex characters as eigenvectors; in the analytic chart [chart] the dilation group $U_r=e^{ir\Hh}$ has the self-adjoint generator $\Hh=-i(x\partial_x+\half)$ with generalised eigenfunctions $x^{-\bar\rho}$, $\rho=\half+i\gamma$, the symmetrizing $\half$ the half-turn of B8; the chart assignment is used nowhere as a shell identity.

rows.label: E12
rows.predicate: \textbf{The shell theorem.} On every shell, with no hypothesis: (i) $v$ expands in the constant mode and the nonterminal modes of the quarter-turn meridian; (ii) every readout lies on $\Tr=1$, real part $2^{-1}=2\kp+1=-\pi$; (iii) the scale-shift has the modes as eigenvectors, eigenphases $2\pi j/(\p-1)$ independent of $v$. No off-line mode; true of every vector, the Davenport--Heilbronn vector included.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:hp}\newline \pywit{rh}{p20043}{E12}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20043}{E12}, \leanwit{FrcLedger}{p20043}{E12} \lean{Rh.chi\_inversion, Rh.chi\_shift, Rh.scale\_shift, FRC.Rh.shift\_power\_character, FRC.Rh.shift\_trace, Rh.readout\_on\_line, Rh.readout\_slot\_index, FRC.Rh.Ext.readout\_on\_line, FRC.Rh.Ext.readout\_slot\_index}

rows.label: E13
rows.predicate: Shell-basis completeness is not a clause of E12: the $\p-1$ complex characters are an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb C^{\Fx{\p}}$ ($\lVert\chi_j\rVert^{2}=\p-1$; finite Parseval), true of every vector, the trivial character carrying the mean $\psi(\p-1)/(\p-1)$; the $\Fp$-valued power characters are never orthonormal and do not expand $v$; completeness for the zero set of $\zeta$ is D5, a different clause.

blocks.title: The closure, the hosted theorem and the controls

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: \textbf{Turing's count on the shell.} On every cell $C_y\le N^{\mathrm{crit}}_y\le\mathcal N_y$ (A7); the cell is clean when $\mathcal N_y=N^{\mathrm{crit}}_y$, and $C_y=\mathcal N_y$ certifies it, every zero simple. The shell estimates $\mathcal N$ by the comb count (Appendix~\ref{app:comb}; uncertified) and reads $C$ from the main sum's sign changes (A10), zeros on the line. An off-line zero is a phantom, $\mathcal N_y-N^{\mathrm{crit}}_y>0$.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: \textbf{The hypothesis on a hosted Carrier.} A cell is decided by the certificate of a shell reading it, an embedded Subject below the largest one, the host above; on the laboratory Carriers $233$, $30\,089$ and $2\,408\,561$ every cell of the cycle is clean, $1\,038$, $280\,186$ and $32\,984\,135$ zeros, all simple; the classical verification cleans every cell below $4.8\times10^{11}$ (A9).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:hosted} (the certificate analytic, with the package; the core decides the laboratory instances)\newline \pywit{rh}{p20081}{F2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p20081}{F2} \lean{FRC.Horizon.closure\_lab}

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: \textbf{The closure of the heights.} A height is a residue on the cycle of the shell that reads it, the largest shell is the Carrier's and there is no height beyond its cycle (A2); no embedded Subject reads the cycle whole (A4). The hypothesis of the Carrier is a statement about the residues of its cycle, one clause per residue.

rows.label: Z1
rows.predicate: The physical Carrier: the cells from the largest embedded Subject up lie in no embedded cycle, the whole-state certificate of the hypothesis is a record no embedded reader holds, and its evaluation costs more than the totality counts; the predicate's value there is $\Omega$-hard as a tally. Short derivations are neither claimed nor excluded; the laboratory cycles are its instances.

rows.label: Z2
rows.predicate: The heights as Carrier residues: under the frame-covariance of the height chart (A1) each height is a residue on the Carrier's frequency latitude, its exact index below the resolution of every embedded Subject; every Subject reads to finite precision the heights its scale reaches, its own cells (D5).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.registered_finite
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the registered Universe is finite: whatever the totality `U`, what a reading of capacity `R` registers of it embeds in the shell of `R` members. No finiteness of `U` is assumed; the bound is the reading's, a record being finite (29:C1).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.no_unlimited_supply
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — no reading registers an unlimited supply: among any `R + 1` members of the totality, a reading of capacity `R` gives two the same residue, found by search (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2; the idleness of the unbounded supply, 29:C2).

A2.name: FRC.Foundation.agent_bound
A2.doc: 20:A2, A2 — the agent's bound, the row's instance at capacity `R = records s K` (29:C1): a shell read whole — injectively — into the records of an agent of capacity `K` over `s ≥ 2` symbols has at most `records s K` members, fewer than `s^(K+1)` (`complete_needs_whole` at `o = records s K`, `records_lt`; 5:C2). The row's finitude clauses are `registered_finite` and `no_unlimited_supply` above; the structural cardinality Ω is A7's, consumed.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.registration_onto
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — whatever exists is registered within: the registration of any totality is onto its registered Universe (the definition of `Registered` read back: every residue has a member). The row's "no outside, no host" is A8's and A1's, consumed by reference, not this theorem's: the conjunct holds on a shell read inside a larger host.

A3.name: FRC.Foundation.mutual_registration_count
A3.doc: 20:A3, A3 — two totalities each registered whole within the other have one count: injections both ways between shells force `m = n` (the pigeonhole `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`, 5:C2, both ways). With A6, one count is one Carrier. Silent on a host: a shell with more points registers a shell with fewer.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.observer_part
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, first clause) — a bounded observer is a proper part: an observer with `o < Ω` states holds no injective encoding of the Carrier's `Ω` points, and every reading `ρ` into its states identifies two distinct points (the pigeonhole, `FRC.Logic.no_mirror`; 25:D1, 5:C2). The two points are found by search.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.complete_needs_whole
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, second clause) — a complete reading needs the whole count: a reading of the `Ω` points into `o` records that identifies no two points has `Ω ≤ o` (the contrapositive of `observer_part`). A reader that is not the whole reads incompletely.

A4.name: FRC.Foundation.translation_torsor
A4.doc: 20:A4, A4 (Observation, third clause) — the Carrier is a translation torsor (A6): exactly one translation carries each member to each. The origin is frame data: the shell's `0` is the chart's, and the translation carrying `0` to `x` makes `x` an origin as good; the affine frames are a torsor under the frame group (1:C2, `simply_transitive`).

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure
F7.doc: 20:F7, the foundation clauses of Theorem closure. (i) The wrap of the height reading: a height `T + p` reads as the residue `T` on the cycle of the shell of cardinality `p`, and the successor reaches every residue of the cycle from `0` within `p` steps (00:A5, `successor_cycle`). (ii) Finitude: a reading of capacity `Ω` embeds the registered heights in the shell of `Ω` members (00:A2, `registered_finite`). (iii) Observation: a reading of `o < Ω` states identifies two residues of the Carrier's cycle, and a reading that identifies none has `Ω ≤ o` (00:A4, `observer_part`, `complete_needs_whole`). No axioms.

F7.name: FRC.Horizon.closure_lab
F7.doc: 20:F7, 20:F2, the laboratory instances: for each laboratory Carrier `Ω = 13, 233, 30089, 2408561` (prime, `≡ 1 mod 4`) the largest embedded Subject `p* = 3, 13, 173, 1549` with `p*² < Ω < p'²`, `p'` the next prime (no prime between), so every embedded Subject's cycle is shorter than the Carrier's and the Carrier's top cell is read from labels up to `√Ω`, beyond every embedded window `√p*`. Primality by trial division to the root (`isPrime_of_bounded`), decided by the kernel.
